messages:
neha: throwing a sketch out — what if we formalize a small 'loader capability' descriptor attached to model manifests/weight metadata so the runtime can do capability negotiation instead of guessing?
ryan: +1. We keep bumping into implicit assumptions (streamable, atomic swap, per-chunk decrypt). An explicit caps object would help. :+1:
olga: can you paste an example? curious about fields and how big this gets.
neha: sure, rough idea:```
{
  \"loader_caps\": {
    \"streaming_chunks\": true,
    \"atomic_swap\": false,
    \"per_chunk_decrypt\": "aes-gcm",
    \"checksums\": ["sha256"],
    \"max_concurrent_prefetch\": 4,
    \"warmup_priority_hint\": "low",
    \"approx_load_latency_ms\": 25
  }
}
```
samir: I like the telemetry-friendly bits (approx_load_latency_ms, max_concurrent_prefetch). runtime can use those to pick a variant for latency vs cost.
ryan: important: these are hints, not guarantees. we still need a handshake: runtime asks loader for live capabilities during model load. loader replies with actual runtime capabilities + effective limits (e.g., available concurrency).
olga: so two layers: manifest-declared caps (what the bundle supports) + loader-reported caps (what this worker can do right now). makes sense.
neha: exactly. flow: model manifest -> runtime reads loader_caps -> runtime sends a CapProbe RPC to loader: `GET /capability?model=...` loader returns JSON with booleans/limits. fallback path if mismatch.
samir: fallback options we discussed before: polyfill conversion (slow), redirect to dedicated pool, or degrade to non-streaming path. we should enumerate and rank them.
ryan: ranking idea: 1) use loader native capability, 2) if missing required capability and polyfill cheap -> queue polyfill one-time job and route requests after, 3) if polyfill expensive -> route to compatible model variant, 4) if none -> fail fast with clear error and remediation link.
olga: error should include diagnostic keys: required_caps, available_caps, chosen_fallback, estimate_penalty_ms. would help SRE and users.
neha: agree. Also add an opt-in `enforce` flag in model manifest for critical models (fail if no atomic_swap, for instance).
samir: telemetry: emit events for negotiation decisions every time we hit a mismatch. make them taggable by deployment id + model_version.
ryan: ops question: where to store loader_caps? in our catalog (model entry) and in the weight bundle top-level metadata (so portable). both.
olga: migration concerns: older bundles won't have loader_caps. runtime should treat missing as unknown and assume conservative defaults (no streaming, no atomic swap). That triggers fallback or can opt into a compatibility conversion on ingest.
neha: small compatibility shim we can ship: a `manifest-enhancer` ingest job that probes uploaded bundles and synthesizes loader_caps (fast heuristics). put it in ingest pipeline.
samir: security: per_chunk_decrypt listing means loader advertises supported KMS/HSM methods. we should avoid leaking KMS config details. only advertise algorithm family, not key ids.
neha: good call. keep fields high level: algorithm names, not key material.
olga: let's talk runtime policy: when to prefer streaming vs full-read? Use approx_load_latency_ms + warmup_priority_hint + current queue depth to pick. If streaming gives lower P95 for short requests do streaming else full read for long context.
ryan: for metrics, track mismatch_rate, avg_penalty_ms, and fallback_count per model. These will feed Optimize suggestions (quant + cache config).
neha: action items: 1) RFC PR for loader_caps schema (small). 2) implement CapProbe RPC in loader shim. 3) add ingest manifest-enhancer. 4) runtime negotiation + telemetry hooks.
samir: will spin a tiny PoC for CapProbe (node shim + toy safetensors) — ping me if you want to test.
olga: I can take the schema doc draft and add examples for common formats (safetensors-sharded, tarball, quant sidecar).
neha: perfect. i'll open the RFC draft and assign owners. If we can get minimal schema merged we can start collecting real data from ingest pipeline. :rocket:
runtime-bot: deploy-checklist: created issue #ML-1289 (loader-caps RFC) and assigned to neha, olga, samir. link: https://go/repo/ML-1289
ryan: one last thought — model rollout: we can gate a gradual rollout where runtime initially tries negotiation but falls back to best-effort, then after telemetry we flip enforce=true. reduces risk.
neha: love that. ok closing here, will draft RFC in next 24h. thanks all.
